findings.issue: Impossible calendar timestamps are silently normalized into different expiration dates.
findings.evidence: Against the in-memory SQLite service, POST {url:"https://example.com",expiresAt:"2099-02-31T12:00:00Z"} returns 201 and persists 2099-03-03T12:00:00.000Z. The analogous April 31 timestamp becomes May 1. Date.parse finiteness only verifies parseability, not the requested calendar date, so links can expire later than the timestamp the caller supplied. Existing tests cover unparseable text and past dates, not calendar overflow.
findings.fix: Validate an explicit ISO timestamp with timezone and verify calendar components before converting it; reject calendar overflow with 400. Add an impossible-day regression.

findings.issue: The default hostname title bypasses the documented 100-character title cap.
findings.evidence: validateLink({url:"https://" + Array(5).fill("a".repeat(30)).join(".") + ".com"}, "https://tiny.test") returns a 158-character title even though supplied titles above 100 are rejected. The default is applied after length validation.
findings.fix: Apply the title policy to the resolved default as well; define and consistently apply truncation for hostname-derived titles, while preserving the documented supplied-title rejection.

reviews.scope: Link storage, analytics, migrations, write rate limits, and SQLite concurrency assumptions

findings.issue: A redirect can credit its click to a different link after its alias is deleted and reused.
findings.evidence: redirectLink reads a link before separately recording by code. A deterministic Node 24 reproduction using the actual SQLite adapter deleted Alice's shared link and recreated the same code for Bob immediately before batch execution. The response redirected to Alice's original https://example.com/ while Bob's replacement row and daily aggregate each gained one click. D1 batch atomicity does not protect the preceding read from alias reuse.
findings.fix: Give every link an immutable unique generation ID, retain it in the initial lookup, and condition both lifetime and daily writes on that ID, ideally keying daily records by the generation ID. Skip the count if the generation no longer exists. Add a deterministic delete-and-recreate interleaving regression test.

Origin values different from request URL origin are rejected, including literal null. GET routes do not mutate management data; PATCH/DELETE require methods unavailable to ordinary cross-origin forms. Missing Origin is allowed by documented contract; no browser CSRF exploit demonstrated.

findings.issue: A single busy code cannot track simultaneous mutations and re-enables pending rows.
findings.evidence: Pause A starts and sets busy=A. Pause B remains enabled because link-list.tsx disables only busy === l.code; starting it changes busy=B while A is still running. Either request finally sets busy="", even if the other is pending. A can then be clicked repeatedly with its stale active value, causing duplicate PATCH writes, rate-limit consumption, and misleading completion messages. deleteLink shares the same scalar and can also clear a running change.
findings.fix: Track pending operations per code using a Set/ref plus state, reject repeated operations for a pending code synchronously, and remove only the completed code. Alternatively serialize all mutations and disable all mutation controls consistently.

findings.issue: A pending deletion writes into whatever confirmation dialog is currently open.
findings.evidence: closeDelete always sets remove=null (line 143); the dialog close button, Escape, backdrop, and Keep link remain usable during DELETE. If A is being deleted, dismissing it and opening Delete B changes remove to B. A success unconditionally calls setRemove(null), closing B; A failure sets deleteError on B. If no replacement dialog is open, failure is hidden entirely because app/page.tsx renders deleteError only inside actions.remove.
findings.fix: Associate each delete result with the submitted code and only clear/update the matching dialog; surface failures outside a dismissed dialog. A simpler option is to prevent dismissal/replacement while deletion is pending and clearly indicate its state.

findings.issue: Successful creation erases edits made while the request was pending.
findings.evidence: create snapshots FormData before the POST, then later calls form.reset() unconditionally. LinkComposer only disables the submit button while saving; destination and advanced inputs remain editable. Typing the next URL/title during a slow POST therefore loses those changes when the first request completes.
findings.fix: Disable the form inputs for the pending create, or preserve edits by resetting only when the current form still matches the submitted snapshot. Keep existing visual design.

findings.issue: The search field has no visible keyboard focus indicator.
findings.evidence: .search input sets outline: none after the equally specific input:focus rule, and no .search:focus-within styling exists.

findings.issue: Selected filter, data source, navigation view, and guide tab states are conveyed only by CSS classes.
findings.evidence: Filter buttons use className selected without aria-pressed or a radio/tab pattern; app/page.tsx lines 65-70, 127-135, 240-250 and workspace-dialogs.tsx lines 116-121 use the same pattern. Screen readers cannot programmatically determine the current selection.
findings.fix: Expose the chosen state using an appropriate semantic pattern, such as aria-pressed on toggle buttons or accessible tabs/radios with their corresponding keyboard interaction.

findings.issue: The click activity graph does not provide its daily values to nonvisual users.
findings.evidence: The SVG accessible name gives only the total and range, while per-day values exist solely in the plotted polyline. Axis text also omits most dates and all corresponding click values.
findings.fix: Provide an accessible daily data table or equivalent text alternative that updates with the selected date range.

findings.issue: On narrow screens an active link is distinguished only by a colored dot.
findings.evidence: The text status badge is display:none by default (app/globals.css:655), while mobile-status text is rendered only for inactive links. The dot's title is not visible by default on touch devices.
findings.fix: Show a textual Active label on mobile alongside the existing Paused and Expired labels.

findings.issue: The search clear control has a very small touch target.
findings.evidence: .search button has zero padding and contains a 14px icon with no minimum size, making its target smaller than 24 by 24 CSS pixels.
findings.fix: Give the clear button a minimum 24 by 24 CSS pixel target, preferably larger, while preserving its accessible label.

findings.issue: Opening a dialog moves focus to the dialog container without a visible focus indicator.
findings.evidence: node.focus() targets the container, but .dialog sets outline: none at app/globals.css:1159; users see no focused element until they press Tab.
findings.fix: Initially focus the close button or another appropriate visible control, or add a visible focus indicator for the dialog container.

findings.issue: A concurrent delete and alias reuse can credit the replacement link and its owner for a redirect to the deleted link's destination.
findings.evidence: redirectLink reads the destination before calling recordClick, but recordClick identifies the instance solely by reusable code. An in-memory SQLite reproduction intercepted db.batch after lookup, deleted Alice's reused alias and recreated it for Bob with a different destination. The response redirected to https://old.example/ while Bob's https://new.example/ link received clicks=1 and Bob's /api/analytics returned that click. The batch's internal atomicity does not cover the earlier lookup.
findings.fix: Give each link instance an immutable identity, carry that identity from lookup into recording, and update both lifetime and daily counters only if the same instance still exists. If it was deleted, skip recording and retain the already selected redirect. Add a deterministic delete/recreate interleaving regression test.

findings.issue: Top links uses lifetime totals without labeling its independent time scope beside the selectable period chart.
findings.evidence: The adjacent chart offers 7/30 days and labels its sum 'clicks this period', but Top links sorts rows by LinkRecord.clicks at line 130 and does not use range or daily counts. A link with only old clicks can rank first even when it has no clicks in the selected period; the heading and values do not explain that these are all-time figures.
findings.fix: Label this panel 'Top links · all time' (and its count scope) or implement per-link period totals if the intended behavior is ranking for the selected range.

findings.issue: Collapsing filled link options silently discards the requested expiration, alias and title on submission.
findings.evidence: Reproduction: enter a URL, expand Link options, enter a title/custom alias/future expiration, click Fewer options, then Create link. The title, alias and expiresAt inputs become disabled at lines 73/82/90. use-link-actions.ts:43 serializes new FormData(form), which excludes disabled controls; lines 53-55 consequently send undefined title/alias and null expiresAt. The resulting link has a random alias and no expiration even though the user only collapsed the section. This is a source-established HTML form submission path, not a browser-run reproduction.
findings.fix: Preserve option values independently of expanded state and include them in the payload when collapsed; use hidden/inert presentation or controlled state instead of disabling configured inputs merely to collapse the UI.

findings.issue: Switching to Activity or Sample erases an unfinished link draft.
findings.evidence: Reproduction: fill URL and optional fields without submitting, click Activity then Links, or Sample then Live. page.tsx:173-179 conditionally mounts LinkComposer only for Links/live. Its inputs are uncontrolled (link-composer.tsx:37-46,69-91), and no draft state exists outside that component. Leaving either condition removes the DOM form; returning creates blank inputs. The normal in-app navigation therefore loses entered destination/title/alias/expiry without warning.
findings.fix: Keep the composer mounted while hiding it outside its view, or lift the draft into stable parent state and restore it when returning.

findings.issue: Resume reports success for expired links without restoring a usable redirect.
findings.evidence: Reproduction: pause an expiring link, let its expiration pass, then choose Resume link. link-list.tsx:194-196 derives the action only from active; the action sends only {active:true} and reports Link resumed. repository.ts:setLinkActive updates only active, leaving expires_at unchanged. presentation.ts:isActive requires expires_at > now, and the redirect contract continues returning 410. A direct pure-function check with expires_at=1/now=2 returned false both before and after active was changed from 0 to 1.
findings.fix: Disable or replace Resume for expired records with an explicit expiration explanation; if renewal is intended, implement an explicit validated expiry update and only claim the link resumed when it can redirect.

findings.issue: Clipboard-denied fallback tells the user to copy the destination URL instead of their short link.
findings.evidence: Reproduction: deny clipboard access and click Copy for a live active link. The catch tells the user to Open the link and copy its address. link-list.tsx:178-188 opens shortPath(code), which follows the public redirect to the destination, so the address bar no longer contains the shareable TinyLink. The displayed short path is itself a button invoking the same failing clipboard API, leaving no usable fallback for copying the full short URL.
findings.fix: On clipboard failure expose the absolute short URL in a selectable read-only field or dialog, allowing manual copying without following the redirect.

reviews.scope: Frontend HTTP client, workspace loading and refresh, health status, mutation lifecycle, and sign-in/error presentation

findings.issue: The health request is coupled to management refresh and mutations in both directions. A stalled health request keeps refresh() pending after link and analytics loading has completed, so successful create/pause/delete actions remain busy indefinitely. Conversely, a stalled management request prevents an already completed health result from updating the status indicator.
findings.evidence: load() waits for Promise.all of links and analytics before reading healthCheck, then awaits healthCheck before returning. refresh() awaits load() (lines 40–44). use-link-actions.ts lines 61–66, 85–90, and 109–114 await refresh before clearing saving/busy; the composer disables Create while saving and link-list disables the corresponding action while busy. Fetch has no timeout.
findings.fix: Update health independently as soon as its request settles and do not make refresh or mutation completion wait for health. Bound or cancel requests where appropriate.

findings.issue: An analytics failure discards a successful links response, leaving the link list and metrics empty or stale, including after a successful mutation.
findings.evidence: Promise.all rejects if either request fails, and setLinks is reached only after both succeed (lines 23–32). load catches and does not rethrow, so the mutation callers continue to show success after refresh even when the updated links were never applied (use-link-actions.ts lines 61–62, 85–86, 109–110).
findings.fix: Handle the two results independently, update each successful dataset, and communicate the failed portion without suppressing the usable links response.

reviews.scope: Read-only focused review of reproducible validation, scripts/verify.mjs, GitHub Actions CI, package scripts/lock hygiene, bounded execution, and evidence provenance.

findings.issue: The advertised five-minute per-check bound has no forced-kill escalation and can hang indefinitely when a child ignores SIGTERM.
findings.evidence: The verifier uses spawnSync(timeout: 300000, killSignal: SIGTERM). A focused local reproduction of the same spawnSync options with timeout: 100 and a SIGTERM-ignoring Node child did not return; an outer two-second SIGKILL bound terminated the reproduction with status 137. docs/delivery.md:47 describes each check as having a five-minute timeout. CI has an independent 15-minute job ceiling, but local npm run verify has no equivalent hard ceiling; a hung process can prevent failed evidence from being saved.
findings.fix: Implement bounded process supervision with a TERM grace period followed by KILL for the owned process group, or wrap each Linux check in GNU timeout --kill-after and provide a portable equivalent. Preserve timeout/signal failure in the verification report.

findings.issue: The configured ESLint check is omitted from the one-command verifier and therefore from CI.
findings.evidence: package.json:13 defines lint and eslint.config.mjs enables Next core-web-vitals and TypeScript rules. The verifier only runs format:check, test, typecheck, build; .github/workflows/ci.yml:19 invokes that verifier. Formatting and tsc do not enforce these lint rules. A separately bounded npm run lint passed locally with exit code 0.
findings.fix: Include lint in the verifier's ordered checks and update the documented check list so future ESLint failures block CI and appear in evidence.

reviews.scope: Bounded independent source review of the 2–3 day URL shortener prototype: creation-to-sharing workflow, failure isolation, and unnecessary product friction. This is a simulated lens requested around Peter Steinberger, not his opinions or endorsement. No architectural expansion is recommended.

findings.issue: A successful create can leave the new short link hidden behind the current list filter, with no persistent result to copy.
findings.evidence: LinkList keeps search and filter in local state (features/links/components/link-list.tsx:50–58). Creating while Inactive is selected necessarily excludes the new active link; an unrelated search does the same. Creation resets the form, refreshes, and only displays a short-path toast, which is cleared after four seconds. Home's onCreated callback only exits sample mode (app/page.tsx:35); it does not reset the list or expose a copyable creation result.
findings.fix: Keep the returned shortUrl in a small persistent creation-success row with a Copy button until dismissed or replaced. This also avoids needing to coordinate list-filter state. Verify creating with Inactive selected and with a nonmatching search.

findings.issue: An analytics fetch failure prevents successful link data from reaching the primary management UI.
findings.evidence: The links and analytics requests share Promise.all, and both state assignments occur only after it resolves. If /api/links succeeds but /api/analytics fails, initial load still shows an empty links array; later refreshes retain stale links even after successful mutations. The backend intentionally isolates analytics-write failure from redirects, but the dashboard couples analytics-read availability to the basic link workflow.
findings.fix: Set link and analytics state independently, or use Promise.allSettled and apply each successful result. Show an analytics-specific failure in Activity while preserving usable links. A mocked analytics failure with a successful links response should leave copy/pause/delete available.

findings.issue: The clipboard failure recovery tells users to copy the destination address instead of the short URL.
findings.evidence: On clipboard rejection the message says 'Open the link and copy its address.' The menu's Open link opens shortPath(l.code) (features/links/components/link-list.tsx:185–189), and redirectLink returns 302 to link.url (features/links/server/redirect.ts:36–38). The resulting address bar contains the original long destination. The displayed short path is a button invoking the same clipboard operation, not a link that offers Copy link address.
findings.fix: On clipboard failure display the full short URL in a selectable read-only field, with instructions to copy it manually. Reuse the existing computed origin plus shortPath; no dependency or elaborate clipboard abstraction is needed.

findings.issue: The 30-day analytics test cannot detect a shortened reporting window or missing cross-link aggregation.
findings.evidence: The fixture contains only one Alice row today and one row 30 days ago; expected output includes today only. A query restricted to today would produce exactly the same result. No row is placed at day−29 (the inclusive boundary), and no second Alice link contributes to the same day to exercise SUM.
findings.fix: Freeze the clock and seed owner rows at today, day−29 and day−30, plus two owned links on one included day. Assert inclusion/exclusion at both boundary dates and the summed owner total. Keep a different owner fixture.

findings.issue: Most byte-limit assertions obtain their expected boundary from the implementation constant, allowing changes to the documented exact 16 KiB contract to pass.
findings.evidence: MAX_JSON_BYTES is imported from shared/server/http.ts and used to construct both the accepted and rejected body lengths. The separate streaming test constrains consumption to five 4096-byte chunks but does not assert an exact 16384-byte limit: for example, changing the implementation constant to 17000 leaves five reads and all parameterized boundary expectations consistent.
findings.fix: Use an independent documented contract value (16 * 1024) in the tests or assert MAX_JSON_BYTES === 16384 before boundary cases. Retain multibyte and streaming cancellation assertions.

findings.issue: The rate-limit test is dependent on wall-clock minute boundaries.
findings.evidence: The test performs 30 writes followed by a 31st and expects 429 without freezing Date.now(). checkMutationLimit keys counts by floor(Date.now()/60000); if execution spans a minute boundary, the final write can validly return 201. The analytics calendar test also obtains today and the cutoff from separate live-clock reads.
findings.fix: Mock/freeze Date.now() for the rate-limit case, then deliberately advance across a minute in a separate reset assertion. Freeze both date sources for calendar-window tests.
